title: Latency signature catalog and alert decision layer for mixed-signal SLOs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently generate burn-rate alerts and paging signals from relatively coarse SLI thresholds (p95/p99 latency, error-rate). These signals are noisy for spiky tail workloads (batchy inference, cold-starts) and are poorly correlated with end-user impact for multimodal routes. The goal of this ticket is to build a lightweight latency signature catalog plus an alert decision layer that combines trace-derived signatures, metric-derived seasonality, and log-based enrichment to produce higher-fidelity burn-rate alerts and smarter paging decisions.

Scope:
- Instrument new trace hooks to capture abbreviated request fingerprints (route, model_variant, batch_size, seq_len_hint, start_time_bucket) without PII.
- Materialize a Latency Signature Catalog service (read-optimized) that stores canonical signatures: expected distribution, typical KV cache hit rate, warmup profile.
- Create an Alert Decision Layer that consumes SLI streams + signature lookup + anomaly score to decide whether to fire burn-rate paging, suppress, or escalate to a lower-tier incident.
- Add dashboards and a playbook: new Grafana panels for signature heatmaps, per-route burn-rate precision/recall, and a paging-suppression simulator to evaluate policies offline.

Out of scope: full retraining of anomaly models, routing-level adaptive throttles (handled in separate ENG ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Trace hook is deployed in runtime sidecar and emits 3 new fields: signature_key, batch_size_hint, seq_len_bucket (no user PII).
Latency Signature Catalog ingests signatures from streaming job and serves 99th percentile lookup latency < 25ms for console queries.
Alert Decision Layer reduces false-positive paging events for a chosen pilot set of 10 routes by >= 45% while maintaining >= 90% recall for high-impact SLO breaches over a two-week test window.
Grafana dashboard panels added: signature distribution heatmap, signature drift tracker, policy-simulation results; links available in ticket.
Runbook updated with suppression rationale and manual override instructions; incident if misfires occur for pilot routes.
Compliance review completed verifying no PII is stored in catalog (security_review_required = true).
tasks: Design trace hook schema and privacy review (Asha + Security)
Implement sidecar exporter for signature keys (Marcus)
Streaming ingestion job (Beam/Kafka) that builds incremental signature aggregates
Signature Catalog read/write API + caching layer (read-optimized TTLs)
Alert Decision Layer prototype (stateless microservice) that joins real-time SLI stream with signature lookup
Offline simulator: replay two weeks of SLI + traces to compare current burn-rate policy vs decision layer
Create Grafana dashboards and Console drilldown panels
Pilot rollout to 10 low-risk routes; collect metrics for 14 days
Postmortem and rollout plan for broader rollout
comments: 2026-03-01 | Asha Patel: Initial draft. Collected requirements from oncall and runtime teams. Noted privacy constraints — must avoid storing full request text. Marked security review required.
2026-03-03 | Marcus Lee: Implemented prototype trace hook and validated payload size impact (~120 bytes/trace). Benchmarked with local load test: <1% CPU increase on sidecar at 2k rps.

2026-03-05 | Data Eng (Lina Chen): Streaming ingestion design doc posted: /confluence/obs/signature-ingest (link below). Suggest using 1-min tumbling windows and compacted topic for signature updates.

2026-03-07 | Asha Patel: Security review kickoff — confirmed hashing + salt approach for signature_key derivation to avoid reversible data. Security suggests retention 30 days for detailed signatures, aggregated indefinitely.
2026-03-09 | Marcus Lee: Deployed Catalog v0 to staging. API responds in 18ms median on staging. Began wiring Decision Layer to fake SLI stream for offline simulation.

2026-03-11 | Marcus Lee: Offline simulator results: pilot routes show 52% fewer pages for transient p99 spikes caused by cold-starts. Two regressions flagged where sustained degradation was suppressed — tuning needed for anomaly thresholding.

2026-03-12 | Asha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require >= 90% recall. Created follow-up tasks to add confidence-weighted escalation when signature drift indicates persistent baseline changes.
